milestone.title: mp install deploys full skill package, not just SKILL.md

intent.outcome: After this ships, `mp install --harness <id>` writes every file under `templates/skills/<id>/` to the harness skill dir (except `manifest.json`, which is install-time metadata read from source). Re-installs are idempotent — stale siblings from removed-upstream files are cleaned via wipe-then-rewrite. `install_project_skill` (project-local deploy) gets the same recursive-walker fix while preserving its current per-file symlink-on-unix / copy-on-non-unix semantics. A new `check_deployment_files` walker is wired into `mp install --check` so file-tree drift surfaces as a warning after every install. New tests in `install_skills_v2.rs` assert that every sibling file referenced by a skill's SKILL.md lands on disk (per-skill link-resolution test); the `check_deployment_files` tests pin both the clean-after-deploy and the missing-sibling-drift paths. INSTALL.md layout diagram and manual install snippet updated to reflect the full-package shape (grep-verified, not line-number-verified).

problem.description: `crates/mp/src/install.rs:755-777` — `deploy_skill_to_harness` hard-codes `let skill_path = skill_dir.join("SKILL.md")` and only ever reads/writes that one file. The same shape lives in `install_project_skill` at install.rs:793-857. The source skill packages under `templates/skills/<id>/` were designed (per M119) as directories that ship every file together, but the deployer was never updated when M120/M121/M122 added deep-dive siblings (`executing.md`, `fixing.md`, `atomic-writes.md`, `flow-stages.md`, `stages.toml`, `planning.md`, `spec-co-design.md`, `reviewing.md`, `DEEPENING.md`, `DESIGN-IT-TWICE.md`, and `scripts/hitl-loop.template.sh` under diagnosing-bugs). After install, `~/.agents/skills/<id>/` contains only `SKILL.md` and every relative link in that file (e.g. `[flow-stages.md](flow-stages.md)` in mp-flow) is a dead reference. Confirmed in this repo: `~/.agents/skills/mp-flow/`, `~/.agents/skills/mp-runner/`, and `~/.agents/skills/diagnosing-bugs/` all contain only `SKILL.md`. The mp-flow SKILL.md references `flow-stages.md` 4× and `stages.toml` 3× — the core skill ships broken to every install. Diagnosing-bugs additionally references `scripts/hitl-loop.template.sh` (2×) inside a subdirectory the deployer doesn't even traverse. There is no test that asserts sibling files land on disk — `install_skills_v2.rs::mp_flow_deploys_across_harnesses` checks SKILL.md exists and contains '12-stage timeline', nothing else. The companion `check_registry` in `crates/mp/src/install.rs:1220+` only validates the source registry — it does NOT walk the deployed file tree, so `mp install --check` reports zero drift even when half the files are missing on disk. This bug was first identified during the 2026-07-12 M158 dogfood pass and deferred from the M156 RC train (original `deferred_reason: 'Not adopting in this cycle'`). Re-groomed 2026-07-15: priority `normal → high` (shipped skills are broken on every install), effort `S → M` (10 ACs + INSTALL.md + reinstall smoke is multi-day work, not small), `execution_status: deferred → in-progress`. The re-groom also resolves the internal contradiction between AC-07 (which required `--check` to flag missing siblings) and the original scope's `No mp install --check enhancement` out-of-scope entry by adding `check_deployment_files` to in-scope.

in_scope: Change `deploy_skill_to_harness` in `crates/mp/src/install.rs` (currently lines 755-777) to iterate the source skill directory and copy every file (recursive, with subdirectory support) to `<skill_dir>/`, except `manifest.json`. Wipe-and-rewrite the destination so stale siblings don't linger. Use the existing `crate::store::atomic_write` (NamedTempFile + persist) per file to preserve the M113 S2 atomic-write contract — no raw `fs::remove` then `fs::copy` race window.
Add `SkillRegistry::skill_source_dir(id) -> PathBuf` method next to `skill_source_path` (currently install.rs:249-254) and update the call site at install.rs:586-587 to use it.

Update `install_project_skill` in `crates/mp/src/install.rs` (currently lines 793-857) — preserve current per-file symlink-on-unix / copy-on-non-unix semantics (this is a documented behavior of the M119 design and changing it would break existing per-project installs). Recurse the source skill dir for each core skill, apply the per-file symlink/copy decision per entry. Update the `SkillRegistry::skill_source_path` reference at install.rs:821 to use the new `skill_source_dir` method.

Add a new `check_deployment_files(source_root: &Path, install_root: &Path) -> FileTreeDrift` function in `crates/mp/src/install.rs` that, for each deployed skill recorded in `InstalledSkillsManifest`, walks the source skill directory (recursive) and compares it against `<install_root>/<harness>/skills/<skill_id>/` (recursive). Report each missing or extra file as a drift finding. Wire this into `check_registry` (or the `cmd_install --check` path) so `mp install --check` surfaces the drift after a full skill-package deploy.

Five new tests in `crates/mp/tests/install_skills_v2.rs`: `mp_flow_deploys_with_deep_dives`, `mp_runner_deploys_with_deep_dives`, `mp_coordinator_deploys_with_deep_dives`, `codebase_design_deploys_with_deep_dives`, `diagnosing_bugs_deploys_with_scripts`. The mp_runner test parses SKILL.md for relative `[<word>.md](<word>.md)` and `[<word>.toml](<word>.toml)` references and asserts each target exists post-install — this is the load-bearing test that makes the bug non-recurring for future skill authors.

One new test in `crates/mp/tests/install_skills_v2.rs`: `check_deployment_files_flags_missing_sibling` — deploys a skill, hand-removes one sibling from the destination, runs the new file-tree check, and asserts the missing file is reported. A second test `check_deployment_files_clean_after_full_deploy` runs the check after a normal deploy and asserts zero drift findings (the happy path).

Update `docs/concepts/02 - Getting Started/INSTALL.md` to reflect the full-package deploy: the layout diagram should show siblings (e.g. `~/.agents/skills/mp-flow/SKILL.md` + `flow-stages.md` + `stages.toml`); the manual install snippet should use `cp -R templates/skills/<id> ~/.agents/skills/` (or `cp -RL` to follow symlinks). Use grep-based verification (no line numbers — those drift with every docs edit).
Run `make test`, `make test-fixtures`, `make doctor` to verify.
out_of_scope: No change to the registry model (manifest.json schema, category, source attribution). M146 already covers that surface.
No change to `~/.agents/master-plan/` template sync — the binary-embedded `templates/` tree is unaffected; only the per-harness skill deploy is fixed.
No symlink resolution semantics for source files (skip symlinks in source — no current skill ships a symlink; revisit if a future skill needs one, e.g. to share a file between skills).

No auto-repair of pre-existing broken installs. Users re-run `mp install` to heal. The new `check_deployment_files` is the read-side companion that surfaces drift; the fix side is the wipe-then-write deploy path above.

No concurrent-install locking. Two simultaneous `mp install` runs against the same destination could race and produce a torn state. Pre-existing limitation, not introduced by this fix; document but do not solve.
No change to `install_project_skill`'s per-file symlink-on-unix behavior — preserve as-is.

design_decisions.choice: Wipe-and-rewrite the destination skill directory on each install (vs. overwrite-in-place).
design_decisions.rationale: If upstream removes a sibling (e.g. M122 drops `atomic-writes.md`), overwrite-in-place would leave the stale file on disk forever — the link in SKILL.md would silently point to a wrong / outdated file. Wipe-and-rewrite matches `store::atomic_write` semantics: each install produces a clean state. Cost is one `remove_dir_all` per skill per install, negligible. Aligns with M146's drift-detection expectation that on-disk state mirrors the registry at install time. Per-file `atomic_write` inside the new dir means an interrupted install leaves a torn state but the next install heals it.

design_decisions.choice: Exclude `manifest.json` from deployment (deploy everything else). Keep it as install-time metadata read from source at every install.
design_decisions.rationale: The registry re-reads `manifest.json` from `templates/skills/<id>/manifest.json` at install time (install.rs:217-228). A stale copy at the destination would shadow registry updates and break M146's drift-detection — the install would record provenance that doesn't match the source the binary actually contains. Alternative (deploy manifest.json too) was considered but rejected: it duplicates source-of-truth on disk with no runtime consumer in any v1 harness (opencode, cursor, pi all read SKILL.md only). If a future harness consumes manifest.json, revisit.

One catalog skill (diagnosing-bugs, M146) already ships a script in `scripts/`. The fix must not regress that path. Symlinks in source are skipped for now — no current skill uses them, and the current single-file deploy didn't either. If a future skill ships a symlink (e.g. to share content between skills), extend `deploy_skill_files` to follow-and-copy or symlink-rewrite.

design_decisions.choice: Apply the same recursive fix to `install_project_skill` (install.rs:793-857), preserving its existing per-file symlink-on-unix / copy-on-non-unix primitive.
design_decisions.rationale: The bug is symmetric between global and project-local deploy paths. If only the global path is fixed, project-local installs (created by `mp init --with-opencode-skill` etc.) keep shipping broken. Per-file symlinks (not whole-dir symlink) match the existing per-file wipe-and-resymlink pattern in that function (the existing code already does `symlink_metadata` + `remove_file` per file).

design_decisions.choice: Copy the source skill directory into the harness skill dir (not symlink the whole tree).
design_decisions.rationale: Two alternatives were considered: (a) recursive copy per-file (chosen), (b) whole-directory symlink from destination to source. (b) would create a single source-of-truth: any change to templates/skills/<id>/ would be live at the destination without re-install. Rejected because: (1) toolchain breakage on Windows / non-unix where symlinks are unreliable (the existing install path explicitly branches on unix); (2) harness expectations — OpenCode, Cursor, Pi all read the deployed files at startup; a dangling symlink (source moved/renamed) breaks every install silently; (3) the source repo's MP_HOME override mechanism (assets.rs:13-45) is the dev-mode 'live link' surface; the install path is for the prod case where MP_HOME is not the repo. (a) is the simplest reliable deploy — atomic_write per file is the existing pattern, the wipe-and-rewrite keeps on-disk state identical to source at every install, and M146's drift-detection gets a clean signal.

design_decisions.choice: Preserve the source file's mode bits on deploy (at minimum: the executable bit +0o111; ideally: full mode).
design_decisions.rationale: diagnosing-bugs ships scripts/hitl-loop.template.sh which is conventionally +x (the source currently has 0o644 per ls, but a future skill could ship an executable). atomic_write writes with default umask, which would silently strip +x and break the script for any harness that invokes it. The fix: after fs::read, fs::write the bytes, then fs::set_permissions(dest, source_meta.permissions()) to copy the mode. Cost: one extra syscall per file. Win: deployed executable scripts work without a manual chmod. Edge: if the destination FS doesn't support unix mode bits (FAT, some network mounts), set_permissions is a no-op — the test (AC-05) skips the assertion in that case via cfg(unix).

open_questions.question: Should `mp doctor` add a check that warns when an installed skill's SKILL.md references siblings that don't exist on disk? Pre-existing broken installs (the current state of ~/.agents/skills/) won't auto-heal on `mp install` upgrade — only on a re-install. A doctor check would surface the problem and tell the user to re-run install. Currently out of scope for M158; could be a follow-up milestone.
open_questions.answer: Out of scope for M158; deferred to a follow-up milestone. The current $HOME/.agents/skills/ may have broken installs that need a re-install, but the auto-heal on upgrade path is sufficient for now.

open_questions.question: Should `install_project_skill` (project-local deploy) use a whole-directory symlink (unix only) instead of per-file symlinks? Whole-dir would be a single op but breaks the per-file `symlink_metadata` stale-detection logic. Per-file matches the existing pattern; whole-dir would simplify the code at the cost of slightly worse staleness handling. Currently the project-local path uses per-file symlinks per the existing pattern.
open_questions.answer: Keep per-file symlinks (matches the existing pattern). Whole-directory symlinks would simplify the code but break the per-file symlink_metadata stale-detection logic; the staleness-handling benefit is worth more than the simpler deploy.

open_questions.question: Wipe-and-rewrite semantics mean a SIGINT mid-deploy leaves a torn destination skill dir. The next `mp install` heals it (re-wipes and re-writes). Should the next install emit a one-line warning when it detects a torn state (e.g. SKILL.md present but a sibling absent), or just silently heal? Silent heal is the current behavior. Warning would surface the issue to the user. Defer to a follow-up if scope creeps.
open_questions.answer: Keep silent heal. The next install always heals a torn destination dir by re-wiping and re-writing; emitting a one-line warning would surface torn state to users but add complexity that can wait for a follow-up if scope creeps.

findings.description: crates/mp/src/install.rs: deploy_skill_files (atomic_write per file, lines 822-868) and deploy_skill_files_per_file_symlink (per-file symlink on unix / copy on non-unix, lines 872-921) are ~95% identical code. The only divergence is the leaf strategy (atomic_write + set_permissions vs symlink/copy). Could be unified into one function with a LeafStrategy enum, with the two helpers becoming thin wrappers. Refactor opportunity, not a bug — flagged for a follow-up milestone if pattern recurs in M168+.

crates/mp/tests/install_skills_v2.rs:install_skills_v2_isolation_grep_gate parses the source file at runtime via env!(CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR) and walks lines looking for #[test] fn declarations. Brittle to source changes (comments containing #[test] or fn , multiline attributes). Filters handle current edge cases (line-start attribute, comment-text #[test], unit_tests mod). Acceptable for M158 spec — the gate fires for any test that calls mp install without an isolation token. Future improvement: parse with syn instead of hand-rolled regex.

crates/mp/tests/common/mod.rs:run_at_repo previously set only MP_INSTALL_DIR (not the MP_*_SKILL_DIR overrides). Existing tests using run_at_repo were therefore deploying skills to the developer real ~/.agents/skills/, not to a per-test scratch dir. M158 fixed this by wrapping isolated_harness_env inside run_at_repo. Downstream impact: the existing install_manifest + suite_install tests (which exercise --toolkit-only and --check, no skill deploy) are now fully isolated too — a defensive improvement, not a regression. Worth noting because the change touched a shared test helper used by every install_* test binary; verified by running install_manifest + install_skills_v2 + suite_install (71 tests, all green).

M-C-2 (round 2 self-review): mp install --check produces false drift warnings when MP_*_SKILL_DIR at check-time differs from MP_*_SKILL_DIR at install-time. Reproducer: install with MP_OPENCODE_SKILL_DIR=/skills-A, then mp install --check with MP_OPENCODE_SKILL_DIR=/skills-B → falsely reports 'deployed skill opencode/mp-flow directory missing at /skills-B/mp-flow' even though the manifest says mp-flow IS deployed (at /skills-A). Root cause: check_deployment_files reads harness::resolved_global_skill_dir(h) at check time instead of capturing the resolved path at install time. Fix: record installed_path on InstalledSkill at deploy time and compare against that, falling back to current resolver only for old entries without installed_path.

M-C-1 (round 2 self-review): check_deployment_files(source_root, install_root) signature is misleading. install_root is silently discarded (let _ = install_root;) — the function uses harness::resolved_global_skill_dir(h) which honors MP_*_SKILL_DIR env, not <install_root>/<harness>/skills/<id>/. Fix: drop install_root parameter and update the cmd_install --check call site; or rename and actually use it.

M-C-6 (round 2 self-review): install_project_skill now wipes pre-existing user files in <project>/.opencode/skills/<id>/ on re-init. Old behavior: only SKILL.md overwritten, siblings preserved. New behavior: fs::remove_dir_all(&dest_dir) + fs::create_dir_all + per-file symlink walk — a user file at .opencode/skills/mp-flow/my-notes.md gets silently deleted. Risk is narrow (mp owns that path by convention) but it IS a behavior change worth fixing. Fix: change wipe from per-directory to per-file — for each dest entry NOT in source, only remove it (preserving any user files); for each source entry, remove dest equivalent if exists then symlink.

L-C-8: SKILL_DEPLOY_SKIP_SUFFIX = ['.swp', '~'] is case-sensitive. On macOS HFS+/APFS case-insensitive mounts, .SWP (uppercase Vim swap) would NOT be skipped. Fix: also match uppercase variants via .eq_ignore_ascii_case() on the suffix.

L-C-10: install() manifest.record_entry falls back to category='core' with empty source attribution if registry.get(skill_id) returns None. Pre-flight check validates is_dir but not registry membership — a skill dir without manifest.json would silently install as core with empty provenance. Fix: bail with a clear error if the skill is in templates/skills/ but has no manifest entry.

L-P-3: deploy_skill_files calls fs::read then fs::symlink_metadata separately per file (two syscalls where one would do). Use a single fs::metadata() handle, derive permissions from it, read bytes via fs::read. Marginal at skill sizes.

L-T-4: deploy_skips_junk_files relies on the synthetic source having a valid manifest.json (id, display, category). SkillRegistry::load silently skips directories without manifest.json — a future refactor that changes the load semantics could break this test silently. Fix: add an inline comment naming the dependency.

L-D-3: INSTALL.md § 4.2 manual install snippet uses 'cp -R' but the header comment mentions 'cp -RL' for symlink-following. Add a second example or footnote showing cp -RL, or mention when to prefer each.

L-T-3: stale_sibling_is_removed_on_reinstall only asserts pre-existing siblings (SKILL.md + flow-stages.md + stages.toml) survive the wipe. Doesn't pin the behavior for a NEW sibling added between deploys — i.e., if source had only SKILL.md at deploy-1 then adds stages.toml at deploy-2, that new sibling should land. Add a test that plants a NEW sibling in source between two deploys and asserts it lands.

L-C-3: collect_skill_drift does not compare file contents for same-name + same-type files. A corrupted install (right name, wrong bytes) would not be detected by check_deployment_files. The walk_verify_artifacts size + TOML/JSON parse catches gross cases. Documented design choice; not fixing — content comparison is out of scope per the M158 spec's design_decisions.

L-C-4: dest.is_dir() follows symlinks. A dangling symlink at the dest falls into the 'directory missing' branch with a misleading message (the dir isn't missing — it's a dangling symlink). Edge case; not fixing — would require a separate symlink check that adds complexity for a rare case.
L-P-4: collect_skill_drift allocates two BTreeMaps per recursion level. Fine for skill sizes (tens of files); would matter at thousands. Not actionable in this milestone — documented and deferred.

L-M-1 (already filed as F-01): deploy_skill_files and deploy_skill_files_per_file_symlink are ~95% identical code, differing only in the leaf strategy. Could be unified into one function with a LeafStrategy enum. Refactor opportunity — not fixing in this pass, deferring to a follow-up.

L-T-1: assert_skill_md_links_resolve is a hand-rolled markdown link parser. Doesn't handle nested brackets, escape sequences, autolinks, or code-fenced blocks. Acceptable for the skill files in practice (they're simple), but a future skill author could break it. Not fixing — deferring to a 'use syn / pulldown-cmark' follow-up.

L-M-2 (already filed as F-02): install_skills_v2_isolation_grep_gate uses hand-rolled source parsing (env! CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR + line scanning). Brittle to source-format changes. Acceptable for the current shape — deferring the syn-based rewrite to a follow-up.

L-M-3: TestEnv::run_at_repo in crates/mp/tests/common/mod.rs is shared by every install_* test binary. The M158 change wraps isolated_harness_env — correct behavior, but the diff doesn't surface that this is a shared-helper change (no commit message yet because the work is uncommitted). Document in the commit message when worktree is committed so future readers know why their test started using isolated harness dirs.

Incomplete skip list: cross-platform and other-editor junk files leak through to the deploy destination, polluting skill dirs and breaking installs. Empirically reproduced on a synthetic skill source containing 'desktop.ini' (Windows folder metadata) and 'foo.swo' (Vim swap continuation): both files are written to the harness skill dir even though the goal of SKILL_DEPLOY_SKIP is to filter OS/editor junk. The shipped test 'deploy_skips_junk_files' only covers the patterns the original author anticipated ('.DS_Store', 'Thumbs.db', '*.swp', '*~') and the round-2 case test 'deploy_skips_junk_files_case_insensitive_suffix' adds only '*.SWP' and '*~' (uppercase). What the test does NOT cover: 'desktop.ini' (Windows folder settings), '*.swo' (Vim swap continuation files — Vim writes both .swp and .swo as paired), arbitrary leading-dotfiles in subdirectories (a test fixture with 'subdir/.hidden' lets the dotfile through — only top-level dotfiles are filtered). The downstream cost is two-fold: (a) a real-world install from a Windows-authored skill source breaks verify_installed_artifacts (size < 1 bytes on desktop.ini); (b) even on macOS, the installed skill dir carries junk files that confuse downstream consumers (skills runtime, doctor checks, future --check drift detection).

findings.description: L51 collision freshly re-created: every AC's evidence string is byte-identical (706 bytes, sha256 prefix a09d05bb). Audited by hashing each AC.evidence field; len(set(evidence for ac in acs)) == 1. AC-01..AC-10 all carry the exact same closure prose 'M158 ship: full skill-package deploy with wipe-then-rewrite...'. The per-step evidence IS unique across 20 steps (good), but the AC layer collapses to one string. Per code-review-lessons.md L51, 'if two ACs have byte-identical evidence strings, at least one of them is lying about its verifier run'. The fix is to re-set per-AC evidence via 'mp milestone criterion pass 158 AC-XX --evidence "<unique per-AC text>"' AND to NOT call 'mp milestone complete 158 --evidence' (per L53/L55 — '--evidence ""' and --evidence with a non-empty string both overwrite per-AC detail). Each AC's evidence should name the specific test that passed (e.g. AC-01: 'cargo nextest run -p mp --test install_skills_v2 mp_flow_deploys_with_deep_dives: PASS'), not a closure summary.

findings.description: Legacy manifest entries (without 'installed_path') permanently reintroduce M-C-2's env-drift false positive. The author's self-finding note 'flagged as a follow-up if the installed-base gets large enough to care' understates the impact — every pre-M158 install on every developer machine hits this fallback path. Concrete repro: existing ~/.agents/master-plan/installed-skills.json contains 9 entries from prior 'make install-opencode' runs (mp-coordinator/mp-flow/mp-runner × {cursor,opencode,pi}) — all lack installed_path. Running 'mp install --check' with a different MP_OPENCODE_SKILL_DIR than the one used at install time will re-read the harness's current resolver and compare against the wrong path, falsely reporting 'deployed skill opencode/mp-flow directory missing at <new-path>'. The structural fix is to write the installed_path for every entry on first install encounter (a 'mp install' run, even a no-op toolkit-only, can lazily backfill the field via a helper), so the legacy fallback becomes reachable only for entries that have NEVER been re-touched post-M158. The docstring at install.rs:530-536 acknowledges the bug exists 'for legacy entries without installed_path (pre-M158-round-2 installs)' — the gap is that no remediation is queued to close the legacy window.
findings.author: agent:external-reviewer

findings.description: assert_skill_md_links_resolve is the load-bearing test that catches the M158 bug class, but it is only invoked for two of the four core-skills-with-siblings tests. Tests that DO use it: mp_runner_deploys_with_deep_dives (line 520), mp_coordinator_deploys_with_deep_dives (line 562). Tests that DO NOT use it: codebase_design_deploys_with_deep_dives (line 591-631), diagnosing_bugs_deploys_with_deep_dives (line 633-...). Both unsuited skills DO have relative markdown links in their SKILL.md: codebase-design references [DEEPENING.md](DEEPENING.md) and [DESIGN-IT-TWICE.md](DESIGN-IT-TWICE.md); diagnosing-bugs references scripts/hitl-loop.template.sh. If a future skill author adds a link to a missing sibling for codebase-design or diagnosing-bugs, the file-presence assertions in those tests will still pass and the regression won't be caught. Fix: add assert_skill_md_links_resolve(&skill_dir) to both unsuited tests so the contract is uniform across all five skill-deploy tests.
findings.author: agent:external-reviewer

findings.description: L13 addendum pattern in deploy_skill_files (install.rs:1046): 'let _ = &meta;' is a dead-reference trick to satisfy the unused-warning linter without using the variable. The meta handle IS used on unix (line 1042: fs::set_permissions(&entry_dest, meta.permissions())), but on non-unix the variable falls out of scope unused. The author added 'let _ = &meta;' to silence the lint, but the cleaner fix is to either (a) move the meta binding inside the cfg(unix) block, or (b) the more honest version: actually use meta for something on non-unix (e.g., a debug log, or assert meta.len() > 0 before reading). Per L13 addendum: 'any #[allow(dead_code)] annotation is a look-here-next flag. Audit the function it's attached to: is there a real call site elsewhere? If yes, the allow is unnecessary. If no, the function is dead and should be removed.' Same logic applies to 'let _ = &meta;' — it's a suppression that hides a structural issue (meta is read on unix but unused on non-unix); the right fix is to drop the meta acquisition on non-unix entirely.
findings.author: agent:external-reviewer

findings.description: The 'AC-01 verification' reads 'cargo test ... mp_flow_deploys_with_deep_dives --no-fail-fast ; ls ~/.agents/skills/mp-flow/'. The 'ls ~/.agents/skills/mp-flow/' half is destructive to the developer's actual install state — when run as part of an automated verifier (mp milestone complete, future CI gate, or any agent that copies the verification string verbatim), it inspects the developer's real ~/.agents/skills/mp-flow/ instead of the test's isolated scratch dir. The right verification for AC-01 is just the cargo test invocation (the test asserts is_file() on the skill_dir internally, no shell ls needed). Per code-review-lessons.md L58 ('verifications that point at one-off shell scripts... must be reproducible from a deterministic source in the repo'), verifications should be either (a) cargo test invocations (the test binary is the contract), (b) mp subcommands (the CLI is the contract), or (c) make targets. An 'ls ~/.agents/...' is a developer-machine-only check; it doesn't belong in a milestone verification string.
findings.author: agent:external-reviewer

findings.description: Test environment isolation gap: install_project_skill_preserves_user_files_on_redeploy calls the public install_project_skill library function directly (not via an mp subprocess). When the developer's shell has MP_HOME exported to anything other than this repo's root (the standard 'make install' landing pad is ~/.agents/master-plan), the embedded registry lookup via SkillRegistry::from_embedded -> assets::toolkit_home reads the developer's MP_HOME and looks for templates/skills/<id>/ THERE — not in the test's source-of-truth. On a stale or empty ~/.agents/master-plan, the loop iterates an empty skill list and panics at the SKILL.md assertion. Empirically reproduced: with MP_HOME=/Users/thiago/.agents/master-plan (default for any developer who ran 'make install'), the test panics with 'SKILL.md must land' because the registry returned ['junk-skill'] (a stale leftover) instead of [mp-flow, mp-runner, mp-coordinator]. The other tests in this file avoid the trap by shelling out to mp (subprocess env is isolated); this test is the only one calling the library directly and was missed. Fix: add a RAII env-var guard (ScopedEnvVar) at the top of the test to set MP_HOME to the repo root. The test was added in M158 round 2 (M-C-6) and the author filed 'fixed' without running it under a non-default MP_HOME — same-session self-review trap (L5).
